In the bustling heart of Tokyo, where neon lights painted the night sky in electric hues and the hum of salarymen echoed through crowded subways, lived a young man named Eon. Fresh out of university with a degree in computer science, he was the epitome of the overworked graduate—bags under his eyes from endless job hunts, a cramped apartment stacked with instant ramen, and dreams of a stable nine-to-five that seemed perpetually out of reach. At 22, Eon was ordinary in every way: average height, messy black hair that he never bothered to style, and a wardrobe of hoodies and jeans that screamed "unemployed millennial." His days blurred into a routine of scrolling job boards, binge-watching anime, and occasional part-time gigs at a convenience store. Little did he know, his life was about to 

It happened on a rainy evening in late autumn. Eon was crossing a busy intersection near Shibuya, umbrella in one hand and his phone in the other, distracted by a notification about yet another rejected application. The world around him was a cacophony of honking taxis and chattering pedestrians. Then, out of nowhere, a blinding light pierced the downpour—not from a truck, as the tropes might suggest, but from a sudden rift in the air itself, like reality tearing at the seams. Eon felt a pull, an invisible force yanking him forward. His phone slipped from his grasp, clattering to the wet pavement. The last thing he saw was the scramble crossing fading into a vortex of swirling colors, and then—nothing.

When Eon awoke, the metallic scent of rain-soaked asphalt was gone, replaced by the earthy aroma of damp soil and wood smoke. His head throbbed as he pushed himself up, blinking against the sunlight filtering through a canopy of ancient trees. Gone were the skyscrapers; in their place stood thatched-roof huts clustered around a dirt road, smoke curling lazily from chimneys. Chickens pecked at the ground, and in the distance, he heard the lowing of cattle. "What the hell...?" he muttered, his voice echoing strangely in his ears. He patted himself down—same clothes, no injuries—but everything felt off. The air was crisp, unpolluted, and the sky a vivid blue he'd only seen in edited photos.

Panic set in quickly. Eon stumbled to his feet, heart racing. Was this a dream? A prank? He pinched his arm—pain, real pain. As he wandered toward the village, a group of villagers emerged from their homes, dressed in rough linen tunics and leather aprons. They stared at him with wide eyes, whispering in a language that sounded like a mix of Old English and something melodic. To his shock, he understood them perfectly. "Stranger! Where did you come from?" one burly man called out, axe slung over his shoulder like a lumberjack from a fairy tale.

The Awakening – Year of the Saintess (Elara at 16)

It began on a midsummer's eve, when the aurora lights danced across the northern skies like veils of ethereal silk. Elara had been helping in the village orphanage that day, as she often did—tending to the sick children with her gentle hands and healing magic that she disguised as "herbal remedies." One boy, little Finn, lay feverish from a wound gone septic, his breaths shallow and ragged. Elara knelt beside him, her white hair cascading like a waterfall of moonlight, and placed her palm on his forehead. She whispered a prayer—not to the pantheon of false gods, but to the one being she truly believed in: her Dad, Eon, the anchor of her world.
